title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 27
paragraphs: In this city Pythius son of Atys, a Lydian, was waiting for the king, and he entertained Xerxes and his whole army with the most magnificent hospitality; he also declared himself ready to supply funds for the war. When Pythius made this offer of money, Xerxes asked the Persians who were with him who Pythius was and how much money he possessed that he could make such an offer. They answered: “O king, this is the man who presented your father Darius with the golden plane-tree and the golden vine; and he is even now, in wealth, the first of all men we know of, excepting you alone.”
